rows.evidence: Re-checked. The back now says only what Proposition 5.4 proves: "It uses V1 + V2 instead of theta. For jointly normal returns with a common per-period Sharpe ratio SR and SR^2 < 2 (Proposition 5.4) it is undersized under positive correlation and oversized under negative correlation. In general it is oversized exactly when theta > V1 + V2." Proposition 5.4 (line 426-428) gives the limit 2(1 - Phi(z sqrt((V1+V2)/theta))), which is below alpha when theta < V1+V2 and above when theta > V1+V2. Re-derived: Corollary 5.2 gives theta = 2(1-rho) + (SR1^2 + SR2^2)/2 - SR1 SR2 rho^2 and V_i = 1 + SR_i^2/2, so for a common SR, theta - (V1+V2) = -rho(2 + SR^2 rho), whose sign is -sign(rho) when SR^2 < 2 (since 2 + SR^2 rho >= 2 - SR^2 > 0). Monte Carlo (4e6 draws, scratch math_checks.py, math_checks_out.txt) confirms the closed form for theta to 0.0035 at the largest deviation across rho in {-0.9,...,0.9} and three SR pairs. No numbers on this card. T is correct.

(1) Grade: the back states a derived result: with SR_n = 0 and a constant omitted cost k the recorded SR is SR_n + k/sigma_n = delta_n > 0 (recorded mean mu + k, sigma unchanged), the estimate converges in probability to delta_n (limiting SR as the lesson defines it), while the luck hurdle sqrt(2 ln N / T) (L01 formula (2), Corollary 2.2) and the Bonferroni hurdle Phi^-1(1 - alpha/N)/sqrt(T) (L02) both tend to 0 like 1/sqrt(T) at fixed N and alpha; so P(SR-hat > hurdle) -> 1. rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/cards.json S7-c212 (L08, new, grade T); course/modules/S/S7/L08.html section 5; key-results row 858
rows.evidence: unchanged since 38e33ad (git diff checked); round-12 evidence: Claim: adding a null trial cannot raise the probability that a genuine configuration wins in sample, whatever the joint law. Proof (re-derived): let X0 be the genuine in-sample statistic and M_k the maximum of k null statistics. The winning event with k nulls is {X0 > M_k}; adding a null Y gives {X0 > max(M_k, Y)}, which is contained in {X0 > M_k}, so its probability cannot exceed the earlier one. No independence or distributional assumption is used. Numerical spot check (scratch scripts/spot_checks.py, 400,000 draws, a common-factor joint law, N-1 = 0,1,4,9,39 nulls): the win probability is non-increasing at every size (for example 0.6448 -> 0.4817 when a second null is added, 0.0513 -> 0.0502 at 39 nulls). The card's back matches Section 5's text. Grade T is right (a proof on the page). PASS. rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L07.html Corollary 5.2 (line 405-410), Proposition 5.4 (line 425-431), key-results rows 747-748
rows.evidence: New row; re-derived and spot-checked numerically (scratch math_checks.py, output math_checks_out.txt). Influence of the Sharpe estimator for standardized return u: psi = u - (SR/2)(u^2 - 1); Var psi = 1 + SR^2/2; Cov(psi1, psi2) = rho + SR1 SR2 rho^2 / 2 (Isserlis: E[u1 u2] = rho, E[u1 u2^2] = 0, E[u1^2 u2^2] = 1 + 2 rho^2). Hence theta = Var(psi1 - psi2) = 2(1 - rho) + (SR1^2 + SR2^2)/2 - SR1 SR2 rho^2, the Corollary 5.2 formula (row 747). Monte Carlo with 4,000,000 draws for SR pairs (0.05,0.05), (0.1,0.3), (0.5,1.0) and rho in {-0.9,-0.5,0,0.5,0.9}: largest |MC - closed form| = 0.0035, consistent with MC error. Sign check (common SR in {0.05, 0.5, 1.3, 1.41}, rho in +-{0.1, 0.5, 0.99}): sign(theta - (V1+V2)) = -sign(rho) for every point. So Proposition 5.4's "undersized under positive correlation, oversized under negative" holds for SR^2 < 2. The limit (line 427) follows from Theorem 5.1, sqrt((T-1)/T) -> 1 and Slutsky's lemma, as the proof on lines 433-436 states; the proof's identity (V1+V2) - theta = rho(2 + SR^2 rho) (line 436) matches the derivation above. PASS.
